description: The FHWA local-agency federal-aid lifecycle — the floor that is true anywhere in the United States because it comes from 2 CFR 200 (Uniform Guidance), 23 CFR (federal-aid highways), NEPA (23 CFR 771), and the Uniform Relocation Act (49 CFR 24).
scope_notes: Your state DOT's local-agency manual (LAG, LPA, LGP, or your state's name for it) implements these same steps and may add its own — this template is the federal floor, not your state's full checklist.
FTA-funded transit projects follow different mechanics (grant agreements, TrAMS) and are not covered by this template.
State and local environmental law (CEQA, SEPA, and their siblings) is a jurisdiction overlay — this template carries NEPA only.

required_evidence.title: STIP/TIP listing or documented exemption — federal-aid projects must be programmed before funds can obligate
Federal program and amount identified (award letter, allocation, or programming record)
Agency standing to administer federal aid (state LPA qualification/certification, or direct-recipient status)
Executed state-local (or federal-local) project agreement
Federal authorization/obligation record for preliminary engineering (FMIS; states name it differently — California calls it the E-76)
Documented PE start date on or after the authorization date — costs incurred before federal authorization are not reimbursable (23 CFR 630)
NEPA class-of-action determination (CE / EA / EIS) with who made it
Signed NEPA decision document (CE determination, FONSI, or ROD)
Resource permits identified with status (401/404, ESA consultation, and similar) — listed, not necessarily issued, at this gate
Plans, specifications and estimate approved by the authority the agreement names
Design standard applied and every design exception, documented and approved
Right-of-way certification, or certification that no acquisition is needed — construction cannot advertise without it
Uniform Act compliance record: appraisal, offer, negotiation, and any relocation records (49 CFR 24)
Utility relocation and railroad agreements status
Federal obligation for the construction phase, dated before advertisement per the agreement's terms

Competitive award per 2 CFR 200.317-327 and 23 CFR 635 — responsive-low-bidder determination and required federal contract provisions (FHWA-1273 on highway work; Buy America; Davis-Bacon; DBE commitment)
Materials certifications and testing records
Certified payroll monitoring record
Change orders with participating / non-participating cost designation — where eligibility quietly leaks on real projects
Final inspection and acceptance record
Final invoice/report of expenditures against the agreement
Single-audit determination for the fiscal year (threshold per 2 CFR 200.501) and a records retention plan (2 CFR 200.334 — retention runs from submission of the final expenditure report)
